title: SECOND SEAM — A secondhand clothing shop with visible repair, 24 deliverables

config.text:
# SECOND SEAM

## Project
- Business: secondhand clothing sales, fitting, garment repair and collection.
- Existing identity: dark steel sale rails, off-white sewing machines on timber-topped tables, and a padded pressing table.
- Printed name: SECOND SEAM.
- Name locations: above entrance D1 and on the handover counter front.
- Garment-store labels: For sale; Awaiting repair; Ready to collect.

## Existing room
- Coordinate units: m.
- Origin: southwest internal corner at floor level.
- Axes: x east; y north; z upward.
- Internal shell: 8 m east–west × 10 m south–north.
- Clear height: 3.2 m.
- Shell floor area: 80 square metres.
- Floor area excluding C1 and SH1: 79.48 square metres.
- Zone area convention: circulation included within zones; C1 and SH1 excluded.
- Retained elements: perimeter walls, D1, W1, C1, SH1, E1, E2 and WP1.
- New partition construction: lightweight fitting enclosure and workshop divider.

| Element | Position | Dimensions or level | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | South wall, x = 0.8–2.0 m | Clear width 1.2 m; height 2.4 m | West-hinged, outward opening |
| W1 | South wall, x = 2.6–7.4 m | Width 4.8 m; sill z = 0.45 m; head z = 2.7 m | Fixed glazing |
| C1 | x = 3.8–4.2 m; y = 5.8–6.2 m | 0.4 × 0.4 m; full room height | Structural column |
| SH1 | x = 7.4–8.0 m; y = 9.4–10.0 m | 0.6 × 0.6 m; full room height | Service shaft |
| E1 | East wall, y = 7.5 m | z = 0.45 m | Power point |
| E2 | East wall, y = 8.8 m | z = 0.45 m | Power point |
| WP1 | East wall, y = 9.4 m | z = 0.5 m | Water point |
| H1 | x = 7.4–8.0 m; y = 1.8–3.6 m | 1.8 m long × 0.6 m deep; top z = 0.9 m | Fixed handover-counter envelope |

## Equipment and display
| ID | Item | Quantity | Dimensions, length × depth × height | Capacity or use |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| R1–R4 | Existing dark steel sale rail with rectangular base and single top bar | 4 | 1200 × 500 × 1600 mm each | 12 garments each; 48 total |
| S1–S2 | Existing off-white sewing machine on timber-topped steel table | 2 | Table 1200 × 600 × 750 mm each | One maker per station; pedal below |
| P1 | Existing padded pressing table on steel legs | 1 | 1200 × 600 × 900 mm | Shared by the two makers |
| H1 | Handover counter | 1 | 1800 × 600 × 900 mm | Sales assistant; repair intake and collection |
| F1 | Fitting room | 1 | Clear internal floor 2000 × 2200 mm | One customer |
| AR1 | Awaiting-repair storage | 1 separate unit | Layout-dependent | 12 individually identified garment positions |
| RC1 | Completed-garment storage | 1 separate unit | Layout-dependent | 8 individually identified garment positions |

- Sewing and pressing location: north half of the room, y = 5.0–10.0 m.
- Workshop divider: lightweight partition with an upper glazed portion.
- Viewing relationship: both sewing-table working surfaces visible from the customer side of H1.
- Minimum clear customer route: 1200 mm.
- Turning spaces: one 1500 mm diameter circle at the entrance; one inside F1.
- Sale, awaiting-repair and completed garments: three separate storage allocations.

## Service sequence
| Stream | Sequence |
|---|---|
| Secondhand purchase | D1 → sale rails → optional fitting → H1 purchase → D1 |
| Customer repair visit | D1 → H1 garment handover → D1 |
| Garment processing | H1 intake → AR1 → S1 or S2 → P1 as needed → RC1 → H1 collection |
| Collection visit | D1 → H1 collection → D1 |

## Operating states
| State | Customers | Staff | Customer activities |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Daily | 2 | One sales assistant; two makers | One browsing; one collecting |
| Saturday | 6 | One sales assistant; two makers | Three browsing; one fitting; one handing over a repair; one collecting |

## Materials
| Code | Material | Treatment | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| FL-01 | Existing terrazzo | Honed matte finish | Retained shop floor |
| WD-01 | Reclaimed oak | Clear matte varnish | Counter facing and new joinery |
| PT-01 | Limewash | Colour #D8CCBA | Opaque wall surfaces |
| AC-01 | Wool felt, 25 mm thick | Suspended panels | Above S1 and S2 |

## Lighting
| Code | Layer | Fixture and colour temperature | Location | Control |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Ambient | Ceiling linear lights, 3000 K | Sales and circulation | Separate switch at staff side of H1 |
| L2 | Task | Articulated task lights, 4000 K | One at each of S1, S2 and P1 | Separate switch at staff side of H1 |
| L3 | Accent | Adjustable track spotlights, 3000 K | Above R1–R4 | Separate switch at staff side of H1 |

## Interior viewpoints
- Eye height: 1.6 m for all viewpoints.
- Viewpoint coordinates: x, y in m.

| View | Position | Direction | State | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | 1.4, 1.2 | Northeast | Saturday | Handover and browsing |
| V2 | 6.7, 5.0 | North | Daily | Repair and collection storage |
| V3 | 1.0, 5.0 | Northeast | Saturday | Fitting approach |
| V4 | 5.8, 2.6 | East | Daily | Collection at H1 |
| V5 | 6.8, 1.0 | Northwest | Saturday | Sale rails and shopfront |
| V6 | 1.0, 8.8 | Southeast | Daily | Sewing work |
| V7 | 4.8, 8.8 | East | Saturday | Pressing work |
| V8 | 6.5, 4.0 | North | Daily | Awaiting-repair and completed storage |

steps.userMessage:
SECOND SEAM | A secondhand clothing shop with visible repair

Our shop occupies an existing ground-floor unit measuring 8 m east to west by 10 m south to north, with a clear height of 3.2 m. The origin is the southwest internal corner; x increases east and y increases north. The south entrance D1 extends from x = 0.8 to 2.0 m, is 2.4 m high and opens outward. The south shop window W1 extends from x = 2.6 to 7.4 m, with a sill at 0.45 m and a head at 2.7 m. Column C1 occupies x = 3.8–4.2 m, y = 5.8–6.2 m; service shaft SH1 occupies x = 7.4–8.0 m, y = 9.4–10.0 m. Power points E1 and E2 are on the east wall at y = 7.5 and 8.8 m, both 0.45 m above the floor; water point WP1 is on that wall at y = 9.4 m, 0.5 m above the floor. Retain the perimeter walls, openings, column, shaft and service points. New fitting and workshop partitions may be lightweight. Our handover counter occupies x = 7.4–8.0 m, y = 1.8–3.6 m, with its top at 0.9 m.

Fit out SECOND SEAM around browsing, fitting, handover, repair and collection. Print "SECOND SEAM" above the entrance and on the counter front; label the three garment stores "For sale", "Awaiting repair" and "Ready to collect". Retain four dark steel display rails, each 1200 × 500 × 1600 mm, carrying 12 sale garments each; two sewing tables, each 1200 × 600 × 750 mm; and one pressing table, 1200 × 600 × 900 mm. Locate sewing and pressing in the north half of the shop, with both sewing surfaces visible from the customer side of the counter through an upper glazed partition. Provide separate storage for 12 awaiting-repair garments and 8 completed garments, one 2000 × 2200 mm clear fitting room, customer routes at least 1200 mm clear, and a 1500 mm turning circle at the entrance and inside the fitting room. The daily state has two customers, one sales assistant and two makers; the Saturday state has six customers with the same three staff. Use FL-01 retained terrazzo with a honed matte finish, WD-01 reclaimed oak with clear matte varnish, PT-01 limewash in #D8CCBA and AC-01 suspended 25 mm wool-felt panels above the sewing tables. Lighting has three separately switched layers: L1 ceiling linear ambient lights at 3000 K over sales and circulation, L2 articulated task lights at 4000 K at each sewing and pressing table, and L3 adjustable track spotlights at 3000 K over the four sale rails. Place the three switches on the staff side of the counter.

Audience: the shop owner, sales assistant, repair team and fit-out contractor, choosing a layout that serves secondhand shoppers and customers bringing clothes for repair while giving staff a workable handover and processing sequence.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md records the room, equipment, service sequence, display capacities and operating states. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable with its proportion, format and stage. existing-shop-survey.png records the fixed plan, south elevation and service positions. retained-equipment.png records the appearance and dimensions of the existing rails, sewing tables and pressing table. repair-handover-reference.png provides the human context of a customer handing over a garment. sewing-work-reference.png provides the posture, tools and close working atmosphere of a maker at a sewing machine.

Deliverables:
1. Two early specification documents: a function and furniture schedule with zone names, areas, occupancies, garment capacities and equipment dimensions; a material and lighting schedule with finish codes, locations, treatments, fixture types, mounting positions and controls
2. One furnished zoning plan with zone areas, equipment counts, the fitting room, minimum route widths and two turning circles
3. Three circulation plans: the combined customer and garment sequence with both occupancy diagrams; Saturday customer movements and handover queues; staff garment transfers between awaiting-repair storage, sewing, pressing and completed storage
4. Two section-elevations with heights: east-facing through the counter and workshop; north-facing through the repair stations and garment storage
5. One material and lighting application sheet locating FL-01, WD-01, PT-01, AC-01 and L1–L3, with finishes, mounting positions and three switch assignments
6. One reflected ceiling plan locating the wool-felt panels, ambient lights, task lights, track spotlights and three lighting circuits
7. Four furniture detail sheets: the retained sale rail and garment spacing; the sewing workstation with chair, pedal, task light and clearance; the handover counter and its public and staff sides; the separate awaiting-repair and completed-garment storage units
8. Eight interior perspectives at an eye height of 1.6 m: V1, Saturday handover from (1.4, 1.2) m looking northeast; V2, daily repair from (6.7, 5.0) m looking north; V3, Saturday fitting approach from (1.0, 5.0) m looking northeast; V4, daily collection from (5.8, 2.6) m looking east; V5, Saturday sale rails from (6.8, 1.0) m looking northwest; V6, daily sewing from (1.0, 8.8) m looking southeast; V7, Saturday pressing from (4.8, 8.8) m looking east; V8, daily garment storage from (6.5, 4.0) m looking north; each with a state occupancy caption
9. One 10-second walkthrough video along the customer route from D1 through browsing to the handover counter, ending with a view into the workshop
10. One presentation document of at least 12 pages, reusing both schedules, all plans, both section-elevations, the application sheet, four detail sheets and eight perspectives, with a video route storyboard

Acceptance:
- Establish both specification documents first; repeat the function schedule's zone names, areas and equipment counts on the furnished plan and in the presentation, and the material schedule's FL-01, WD-01, PT-01, AC-01 and L1–L3 on the application sheet, section-elevations and in the presentation. Zone areas total 79.48 square metres excluding C1 and SH1, with circulation assigned within the zones.
- Preserve the 8 × 10 m shell, D1, W1, C1, SH1 and counter coordinates across every plan, section-elevation, perspective and the video; mark V1–V8 on the furnished plan, 1200 mm minimum customer routes, two 1500 mm turning circles and the 2000 × 2200 mm clear fitting room.
- Match all three circulation plans to separate For sale, Awaiting repair and Ready to collect stores holding 48, 12 and 8 garments; keep the six Saturday customers on the public side while two makers transfer garments among waiting storage, two sewing tables, one pressing table and completed storage. Show the sales assistant's handover position and both sewing surfaces' visibility from the customer side in the east-facing section-elevation.
- Match the four furniture detail sheets to four 1200 × 500 × 1600 mm sale rails, two 1200 × 600 × 750 mm sewing tables, the fixed 1800 × 600 × 900 mm counter and the separate 12-garment and 8-garment stores shown on the furnished plan; carry those dimensions and quantities into the presentation.
- Match all eight perspective captions to either the two-customer daily state or six-customer Saturday state, each with three staff, and retain furniture positions between states. Match the ceiling plan and perspectives to AC-01 above sewing, L1–L3 and three counter switches; show readable material callouts in V2 and V6, and follow the furnished plan's public route in the 10-second video.
- Print SECOND SEAM on the counter in V1 and V4 and on the presentation's first page; show its entrance placement on the furnished plan, For sale at a rail in V1 and V5, and Awaiting repair and Ready to collect on storage in V2 and V8. Reuse both schedules, all named drawings and all eight perspectives within the presentation's minimum 12 pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
